title: Mouse CosMx Example
text: mouse object single tissue, rather selecting one sample spatial coordinates cropped rectangular window centered tissue sized retain roughly 5,000 cells. Since crop contiguous, local neighborhoods cell density preserved. feature matrix stored "layer 1" layer single sample_id label added. Edit target_cells change crop size.
code: adata_full <- anndata$read_h5ad(brain_path)  coords <- py_to_r(py_get_item(adata_full$obsm, "spatial"))[, 1:2, drop = FALSE] x <- coords[, 1] y <- coords[, 2]  # Size a square window, centered on the tissue, to capture ~target_cells. n_total <- nrow(coords) frac    <- min(1, target_cells / n_total) cx      <- median(x) cy      <- median(y) half_x  <- (diff(range(x)) / 2) * sqrt(frac) half_y  <- (diff(range(y)) / 2) * sqrt(frac)  in_window <- x >= (cx - half_x) & x <= (cx + half_x) &              y >= (cy - half_y) & y <= (cy + half_y)  cat("Cells kept:", sum(in_window), "of", n_total, "\n")  py$adata_full <- adata_full py$in_window <- r_to_py(which(in_window) - 1L)   # 0-based indices for Python adata <- py_eval("adata_full[in_window].copy()", convert = FALSE)  # Store the feature matrix as a named layer and add a sample label. py_set_item(adata$layers, "layer 1", adata$X) n_cells <- as.integer(py_to_r(adata$n_obs)) py_set_item(adata$obs, "sample_id", r_to_py(rep("mouse_brain", n_cells)))  adata$write_h5ad(h5ad_path, compression = "gzip") adata

title: repSpatWorkshop
text: Landing page: https://amanpreet60.github.io/repSpat_Workshop/index.html. workshop demonstrates use Python implementation repSpat within R reticulate package. RepSpat detects repeated spatial patterns spatial omics data, defined spatially separated tissue regions similar distributions features, gene expression, cell types, binary markers, molecular cellular measurements. repSpat provides nonparametric statistical inference framework based spatially constrained clustering followed multiple hypothesis testing clusters using maximum mean discrepancy squared (MMD²) statistic block-permutation procedure. enables formal hypothesis testing repeated spatial patterns. Python implementation repSpat accepts input data AnnData (.h5ad) format, widely used data structure single-cell spatial omics analyses. Bioconductor users, SpatialExperiment objects can readily converted AnnData format within R analysis. Python package available GitHub, workshop demonstrates use functionality R reticulate package.
